newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli government to sell venture capital fund.
newsitem.headline: Israeli government to sell venture capital fund.

text.p: The Israeli Government Corporations Authority published an offering on Wednesday to sell its Yozma venture capital fund.

The authority set a November 24 deadline for applications. Prior to the sale, Yozma's holdings in nine venture capital funds will be transferred to the government, leaving it with $10 million in direct holdings in high-tech companies.
Yozma was formed in 1992 to encourage venture capital investment in Israel and help create employment for immigrants from the former Soviet Union then streaming into the country.

Yozma invested $60 million over the next four years in nine venture capital funds, taking a 40 percent stake in each, and another $10 million directly in companies. All told, it helped leverage $200 million in investments.

But in recent years, the venture capital industry has thrived on its own, with more than $1 billion in capital raised. As a result, the Treasury concluded direct government intervention was no longer needed and won approval from the parliamentary Finance Committee earlier this week to sell Yozma.
